title: Midway Geyser Basin / Firehole ecological authoring catalogue
geographic_scope: Meter-scale authored Midway segment and explicitly labeled future Yellowstone extensions.
status: Research catalogue and implementation plan. Entries are not a runtime spawn list or a claim that assets and behavior are implemented.

world_contract.placement: Every final transform, habitat polygon, perch, route and water connection is authored or explicitly approved and serialized.
world_contract.runtime_randomness_allowed: Only bounded behavior variation of persistent authored entities, never new terrain, habitat polygons or species placement.

evidence_classes.documented_site: Source explicitly names Midway or a particular feature. Does not locate every individual.
evidence_classes.documented_corridor: Source establishes Firehole river/drainage use; exact local patch unknown.
evidence_classes.documented_park: Yellowstone presence; local suitability and occurrence must be reviewed.
evidence_classes.habitat_inference: Functional guild or proposed relationship inferred from habitat. Not a species-level locality record.
evidence_classes.documented_elsewhere: Evidence concerns a different Yellowstone site or research system; expansion only.
evidence_classes.dated_nondetection: Defined site survey did not detect organism at a particular time; not permanent absence.

sources.description: NPS, Grand Prismatic Spring, updated 2026-08-15. Feature size, spring behavior, microbial interpretation.
NPS, Excelsior Geyser Crater. Crater dimensions and continual Firehole discharge.
NPS, Forests, updated 2025-04-18. Forest types, lodgepole form, selected understory.
NPS, Influence of Geology. Substrate and vegetation relationships.
NPS, Ecological Consequences of Fire. Lodgepole regeneration and landscape history.
NPS, Wetlands, updated 2025-04-18. Wetland distinctions; Firehole Lake Road observations.
NPS, Hydrothermal Plant Communities, updated 2025-04-18. Thermal shifts and vegetation.
NPS, Yellowstone Sulphur Flower, updated 2025-04-18. Explicit Midway presence and suitable ground.
NPS, Ross's Bentgrass, updated 2025-04-18. Distribution, calendar, and qualified dispersal hypothesis.
NPS, Wildflowers. Broad habitat and flowering guidance.
NPS, Bison Ecology. Diet, behavior, movements, and grazing interactions.
NPS Old Faithful Virtual Visitor Center, Bison. Firehole/Madison winter use; historical interpretation.
USGS YVO, Wildlife in Yellowstone National Park's Thermal Basins, 2024-12-16. Thermal biota and Firehole elk context.
NPS, Elk. Park species and broader ecological context.
NPS, American Dipper, updated 2025-04-17. Aquatic-insect foraging.
NPS/MSU Acoustic Atlas, American Dipper & Canada Geese, recording dated 2014-02-26. Explicit Firehole observation.
NPS, Birds, updated 2026-02-04. Park presence, seasons, and habitat differences.
NPS, Raven. Park corvid reference.
NPS, Red Squirrel, updated 2025-04-17. Conifer habitat and midden behavior.
NPS, Montane Vole, updated 2025-04-18. Meadow habitat and prey role.
NPS, Coyote. Small-mammal feeding and habitat.
NPS, Fish Ecology, updated 2026-02-02. Native versus introduced fish and Firehole context.
Kaya, Kaeding & Burkhalter, Use of a Cold-Water Refuge by Rainbow and Brown Trout in a Geothermally Heated Stream, 1977. Historical Sentinel Creek field evidence; publisher abstract available.
NPS, Boreal Chorus Frog, updated 2025-04-29. Quiet breeding water and calling season.
NPS, Columbia Spotted Frog, updated 2025-04-29. Habitat and life stage.
NPS, Terrestrial Gartersnake, updated 2025-04-29. Habitat and diet.
NPS, Thermophilic Eukarya, updated 2025-04-18. Thermal flies and plant/fungal examples.

Willemssens et al., Habitat Characteristics, Distribution, and Abundance of Cicindelidia haemorrhagica in Yellowstone National Park, *Insects* 15:15, 2024, DOI 10.3390/insects15010015. Tables distinguish detections from 2016 nondetections.

Adams et al., Heavy metal movement through insect food chains in pristine thermal springs of Yellowstone National Park, *PeerJ*, 2024, DOI 10.7717/peerj.16827. Rabbit Creek and Dragon–Beowulf study context.
NPS, Bats, updated 2025-04-18. Insectivory, roosting, and seasonal activity.
NPS, Beaver. Habitat engineering, gradients, food, and bank dens.
NPS, River Otter, updated 2025-04-18. Water association and behavior.
USGS YVO, Where the pigment ends, 2021-12-27. Temperature, chemistry, and photosynthetic limits.
Willemssens et al., Hot springs, cool beetles, *Annals of the Entomological Society of America* 118:237–243, 2025. Heat-reflection and physiology study.
Márquez et al., A virus in a fungus in a plant: three-way symbiosis required for thermal tolerance, *Science* 315:513–515, 2007, DOI 10.1126/science.1136237. Experimental symbiosis reference.
USGS station 06036805, Firehole River at Old Faithful. Calibration-data discovery point; not Midway measurement.
USGS station 06036905, Firehole River near West Yellowstone. Calibration-data discovery point; not Midway measurement.
NPS 2026 river fishing-temperature restriction updates. Contemporary evidence of heat stress; page incorporates several dated updates.
NPS, Research Report: Pollinator Hotshot Crews, updated 2017-08-24. Observation variables and research approach.

Marshall, Hobbs & Cooper, Stream hydrology limits recovery of riparian ecosystems after wolf reintroduction, *Proceedings B* 280:20122977, 2013, DOI 10.1098/rspb.2012.2977. Northern-range experiment; geographical transfer requires caution.
Hall, Dybdahl & VanderLoop, Extremely high secondary production of introduced snails in rivers, *Ecological Applications* 16:1121–1131, 2006. Firehole included; abstract-level food-web finding.
NPS, Hydrothermal Systems, updated 2025-04-18. Dynamic features and 2024 Biscuit Basin event.
NPS, Sagebrush-steppe. Regional extension habitat distinctions.
NPS Amphibians; Yellowstone presence and widespread species; exact Midway sites unspecified.
NPS Trumpeter Swan; park species reference; does not establish a Midway nest.
NPS Insects as a Vital Sign in the GYE; pollination guilds and phenology.

dated_nondetections.effort: At least 15 minutes per inspected site in late July 2016, per study Table 2.
dated_nondetections.interpretation: Do not claim present at these specific features from this study; nondetection does not prove permanent absence.
dated_nondetections.placement_policy: Exclude as a routine baseline occupant; require new site evidence to override.

hard_rules.rule: No fish in Grand Prismatic, Excelsior, Opal or Turquoise hot-pool habitats; fish route graphs are river-only.
Do not identify a microbial species, temperature or toxicity from visible color alone.
Do not invent a cold tributary at Midway to implement Sentinel Creek refuge behavior; use verified connected water or allow fish to leave.
Every patch checks phenology and life stage; Ross’s bentgrass is not a lush default July plant.
The catalogue never causes every listed taxon to spawn; accepted authored placements are separate data.
No automatic Midway beaver colony, dam, frog pond or swan nest.
A future trophic cascade model must include habitat, browsing, hydrology, time scale and multiple interacting drivers.
Store surface, water, root-zone and animal-body temperatures as distinct quantities.

Fish presence by reach and temperature; local cold-refuge connectivity.

Local insect taxa, thermal tolerances and emergence schedules.
